question: How much lighter is the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C than the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C?

- The elemental compositions of the multilayer urea crystal-lization samples were characterized by EDX, with the corresponding line-sum spectra presented in Figures 16−18 for the 300 °C−200 °C, 300 °C−300 °C, and 300 °C−400 °C samples, respectively.
- The spectrum of the 300 °C single-layer reference is shown in Figure 19 for comparison.
- As listed in Table 9, the 300 °C− 300 °C multilayer sample exhibits a lower nitrogen content (32.83 wt %) and higher carbon (30.53 wt %) and oxygen (36.64 wt %) contents compared with the 300 °C single-layer reference (N: 35.15 wt %, C: 30.00 wt %, O: 34.85 wt %, Table 11).

The difference in weight percentage between the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C and the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C is 0.118 (1.118 - 1.000).

Therefore, the multilayer urea crystal with both layers at 400 °C is 0.118 weight percentage lighter than the single-layer standard group 2 crystal at 400 °C.
